newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-STEVE WAUGH HOLDS UP SOUTH AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-STEVE WAUGH HOLDS UP SOUTH AFRICA.

text.p: A defiant undefeated 51 from Steve Waugh held up South Africa but Australia still found themselves on the brink of defeat at lunch on the fourth day of the third and final test at Centurion Park on Monday.

Waugh, who began the day 24 not out, lost three partners as Australia stuttered to 160 for seven in their second innings, a lead of just three runs over South Africa who were bowled out for 384 in their first innings.
The day began disastrously for Australia, who already have an unbeatable 2-0 lead in the series, when Greg Blewett was bowled by a fast inswinging yorker from Allan Donald in the first over.

Michael Bevan was then bowled behind his legs as he injudiciously tried to sweep off-spinner Pat Symcox and it became 131 for seven when Ian Healy was scooped up down the leg side by wicket-keeper Dave Richardson off Brett Schultz.

Healy stood disbelievingly with hand on hip and glowered at South African umpire Cyril Mitchley when he belatedly raised his finger. Healy then marched angrily from the field, throwing his bat through the dressing room door.
Replays suggested Healy might have been justified in his view that the ball had flicked his pad rather than bat on its way to Richardson.
Waugh edged a ball from Schultz over the slips when he had reached 31 and was missed two runs later when Brian McMillan was unable to hold a bat-pad chance at silly-point off the bowling of Symcox.
He survived and, with partner Shane Warne (11 not out) also lucky to escape when he was dropped on nought by Donald diving forward at mid-on, had added 29 for the eighth wicket at the interval.
